text: After this you can prepare a defensible audit outcome and action record.

Completing an audit takes more than a pass label. Record scope, evidence, findings, conditions and the responsible authority. Corrective actions need owners, expected outcomes and confirmation evidence. An overall acceptance decision does not erase an open observation. Store the resulting report so future teams can reconstruct what was decided and what remained unresolved.

items: Reconcile the finding list with notes and evidence. You should see: Material issues have not disappeared between drafts. If not: Ask reviewers about missing or merged items.
Document the disposition and all conditions. You should see: The decision has a named authorized role. If not: Do not treat tentative agreement as final authorization.
Assign actions and verify their results. You should see: Closed actions have supporting evidence. If not: Keep incomplete actions open with the next step visible.
Release the final report with the correct version. You should see: The organization has a traceable record. If not: Retain superseded drafts only as required by the local record rules.
The example product review could accept a release conditionally while an identification label is corrected. The report should show the condition until its correction is verified.

text: Close a finding when evidence supports its disposition, not when its owner promises to fix it.
Organizations may define different formal outcome terms and sign-off routes.

items: Deleting a finding after conditional approval Future teams lose the reason for the condition. Fix: Keep the finding and link it to closure evidence.
